baa_10y_spread.proxy_note: Moody's Baa corporate bond yield minus the 10Y Treasury -- a long-run investment-grade credit-risk-premium PROXY, not the literal ICE BofA IG OAS series this system quotes daily. Real history back to 1986. Useful for direction and episode timing (did credit broadly tighten/widen, and when); its magnitude runs tighter than IG OAS and far tighter than HY OAS, so never quote its level as if it were either.
baa_10y_spread.label: quiet lately, historically extreme

history_digest.sentence: The 10-year Treasury yield (5.22%) has been at or above this level since Sep 28; before this run, the last time was Jun 2007, and only briefly (7 readings); it was last there routinely until May 2002. This run's high was 5.31% on Oct 5, last matched in May 2002. Today's reading is higher than on 87 of every 100 days of the last 30 years, but about average (49th percentile) since 1962.

The 10-year TIPS real yield (2.92%) has been at or above this level since Sep 30; before this run, the last time was Nov 2008, and only briefly (17 readings). This run's high was 2.95% on Oct 5, last matched in Nov 2008. Today's reading is higher than on 99.7 of every 100 days since 2003. But TIPS only exist since 2003: the Cleveland Fed's model real rate, which reaches back to 1982, puts real rates at the 54th percentile since 1982 (80th over the last 30 years) — high against the last two decades, not against the 1980s and '90s.

10-year real yields in their top tenth while the Baa credit spread sits in its bottom tenth (both measured since 2003, when TIPS data begins): true since Jun 17; it happened twice before — Apr 2006–Jul 2007 (recession began 21 months after it started; S&P 500 +14.5% over the next 12 months); Apr 2024–Jan 2025 (too recent to judge; S&P 500 +4.4% over the next 12 months). Two cases are an anecdote, not a pattern. At a looser top-fifth/bottom-fifth cut, today's stretch reaches back to Sep 2023.

The 10-year Treasury yield is up 104bp this year — the 9th-largest rise through this date in 64 years (bigger: 1987 +263bp, 1981 +257bp, 2022 +237bp, …). A 12-month rise this big (+1.09 points) has started 14 times since 1963. Measured from each start, the S&P 500 (price only) was lower a year later in 5 of 14 (any 12-month stretch since 1962: 24.4%), and a recession began within two years in 6 of 13 (any two-year stretch since 1962: 26.0%; 1 more began mid-recession).
